finding.summary: No magnitude clamp on parsed row/column when resolving ranges — grammar admits arbitrarily large row numbers
finding.evidence: `fragment ROW: '$'? [1-9][0-9]* ;` places no digit limit on a row, and `resolveRange` (coordinates.ts) parses it with `r: match[2] ? parseInt(match[2], 10) : null` and passes it straight to `toRange` with no upper bound / sheet-dimension check. A single short input such as `=SUM(1:99999999999999)` or `=COUNT(A1:B99999999999)` produces a Range spanning ~1e14 rows, which `toSrefs` in `buildDependantsMap` / `Arguments.iterate` then iterates one sref at a time — an effectively non-terminating loop that freezes the tab. The new `REFRANGE` alternatives (`ROW ':' ROW`, `REF ':' ROW`, …) widen the set of short inputs that reach this unvalidated path, and `resolveRange` is the natural place to clamp to the sheet's maximum dimensions but does not.
